hints: Look closely at what a potometer actually tracks, the movement of an air bubble along a capillary tube as water is taken up by the shoot.
Remember that any rate means amount divided by time, so ask yourself what amount (distance, area or volume?) is being divided by minutes here.
walkthrough:
**Recall what a potometer measures**

Think of the potometer as a water tracker. As the leafy shoot transpires, it pulls up water and the air bubble moves along the scale.

We measure how much water is taken up, which is a volume.

**Apply the idea of rate**

A rate is always amount per unit time. For transpiration, that is volume of water per minute.

$$\text{rate} = \frac{\text{volume of water taken up}}{\text{time}}$$

**Put the correct units together**

Volume is measured in $cm^3$ and time is measured in $min$. Per minute is written as $min^{-1}$.

So the units are $$cm^3 \, min^{-1}$$ which matches option D.

options.A: This reads as $cm$ times $min$, not per minute, so it is not a rate at all.
options.B: This is area per time ($cm^2 \, min^{-1}$). A potometer measures volume of water, not leaf area.
options.C: This mixes volume with per gram per minute incorrectly and has time on top ($min$ not $min^{-1}$), so it is not volume per time.
options.D: This is volume per time ($cm^3 \, min^{-1}$), exactly what a potometer measures as water uptake per minute.
